3.happening: We count the indices as n = {n}.
3.why: The scan and jump ranges are bounded by n.

4.happening: We mark every index as not-yet-reachable.
4.why: Reachability is proven one index at a time from the right.
4.invariant: A False cell means 'cannot yet prove it reaches the end'.

5.happening: We mark the last index reachable.
5.why: The end reaches itself with no jump.

6.happening: We start the scan at index {i}.
6.why: Every index left of the end must be decided.
6.invariant: Indices right of i are already decided.

7.why: Its reachability depends on already-decided indices to its right.

7.happening: The scan passed index 0, so every index is decided.
7.why: There is nothing left to the left of 0.

8.happening: From index {i} a jump can land as far as index {reach}.
8.why: nums[i] is the maximum jump length from here.
8.invariant: reach never exceeds the last index.

9.happening: We begin probing at the first neighbour after i.
9.why: Any reachable neighbour in range makes i reachable.

10.happening: Probe neighbour {j}, still within i's jump range.
10.why: We look for one neighbour that already reaches the end.
10.invariant: j never leaves i's jump range.

10.happening: No neighbour in range reaches the end, so i cannot either.

11.why: Jumping i to j then continuing reaches the end.
11.invariant: One reachable landing spot is enough.

11.happening: Neighbour {j} does not reach the end.

12.why: It can jump to a neighbour that reaches the end.
12.invariant: A reachable cell turns green and never reverts.

13.happening: We stop probing — one good neighbour is enough.
13.why: Reachability is a yes/no fact; extra probes add nothing.

14.happening: We advance the probe to the next neighbour.
14.why: The previous landing spot was unreachable.
14.invariant: Probing only moves rightward within the range.

15.happening: We move the scan left to index {i} - 1.
15.why: The next index to decide is one to the left.
15.invariant: Decided indices accumulate on the right.

16.happening: We read the answer from index 0's reachability.
16.why: The question is whether the start can reach the end.

17.why: It says whether index 0 reaches the last index.
17.invariant: The verdict follows from fully-computed reachability.

init.happening: Mark the end reachable and everything else unknown.
init.why: Backward DP seeds from the goal.
init.invariant: Only the last index is known reachable at first.

loop.happening: Scan an index or probe its jump range.
loop.why: Each index's reachability is derived from its neighbours.
loop.invariant: Indices are decided right to left.

update.happening: Compute a jump range or mark an index reachable.

move.happening: Advance a probe or the scan cursor.

check.happening: Test whether a neighbour reaches the end.
check.why: One reachable neighbour proves the current index.

return.happening: Return whether the start reaches the end.
